title: Money Town
tagline: Why money exists, and what it really is
principle: Money as a concept and instrument
philosophy: Money is a tool, not the goal

lessons.title: Before money: the barter mess
lessons.subtitle: Why swapping stuff was so hard

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Long before coins and UPI, people swapped stuff. It was called barter.

steps.title: Get the cricket bat
steps.caption: You have mangoes. You want a cricket bat. Tap a villager to trade with them.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Ugh! I just wanted a bat. Why did I need a chicken first?!

options.text: Both people had to want what the other had
options.why: Exactly. Economists call it the 'double coincidence of wants'. Money fixes it, because everyone accepts money.
Mangoes are valuable! The problem was finding someone who had a bat AND wanted mangoes.
Markets existed. The hard part was matching what each person had with what they wanted.

steps.question: A farmer has rice and wants shoes. The shoemaker only wants milk. What does money let the farmer do?

options.why: That's barter thinking! With money, the farmer skips the cow entirely.

options.text: Sell rice to anyone, then pay the shoemaker
options.why: Yes! Money splits one hard swap into two easy ones: sell to anyone, buy from anyone.

options.text: Wait until the shoemaker wants rice
options.why: That could take forever. Money means nobody has to wait for a perfect match.

steps.title: Money is a shared agreement
steps.realLife: Money works because everyone agrees to accept it. That one agreement makes trade fast: sell to anyone, buy from anyone.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Money has three jobs. Anything that can do all three can work as money.
Tap each one to see it in action.

items.title: Medium of exchange
items.text: Everyone accepts it in trade. You pay ₹40 for a samosa plate, no mangoes needed.

items.title: Unit of account
items.text: It measures value. A bat costs ₹800 and a chai ₹20, so you can compare anything with anything.

items.title: Store of value
items.text: It keeps value over time… mostly. Spoiler: a sneaky villain called The Melt is coming in World 1.

steps.question: Your bat costs ₹800 and a phone costs ₹16,000. Which job lets you say the phone is worth 20 bats?

options.why: That job is about paying. Comparing prices is a different job.
Right! Money is a measuring stick for value, so ₹16,000 ÷ ₹800 = 20 bats.
That job is about keeping value over time, not comparing things today.

steps.question: Why would tomatoes make terrible money?

options.text: They rot, so they can't store value
options.why: Yes. Good money has to last. Tomatoes fail the store-of-value job within a week.
Cheap isn't the problem; coins are cheap too. The problem is they rot.
Lots of people love tomatoes! They just can't keep their value over time.

steps.title: The rupee's weak spot
steps.realLife: The rupee does all three jobs in India. Its weakest job is store of value, because prices rise over time. You'll see exactly why in World 1.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Wait. My money is just numbers on my phone now. Is it even real?

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Great question! Money keeps changing form. What matters is that people trust it.

items.title: Shells and metal
items.text: Cowrie shells, then metal coins. Hard to fake and easy to carry.

items.title: Paper notes
items.text: Every Indian note carries a printed promise signed by the RBI Governor: "I promise to pay the bearer…"

items.title: Bank money
items.text: Most money today is just numbers in bank accounts, not notes in wallets.

items.title: UPI
items.text: UPI moves bank money between accounts in seconds. It's a super-fast road, not a new kind of money.

steps.question: When you pay ₹50 by UPI, what actually moves?

options.text: A digital coin owned by the app
options.why: UPI apps don't own your money. They send instructions between banks.

options.text: Money from your bank account to theirs
options.why: Yes. UPI is a payment rail between bank accounts. The money underneath is still rupees in banks.
It's not a loan. Real rupees leave your account and land in theirs.

steps.question: A ₹500 note costs only a few rupees to print. Why is it worth ₹500?

options.text: It's swapped for gold in a vault
options.why: Not anymore. You can't swap notes for gold. Modern money is 'fiat': its value comes from trust and law.
The ink helps stop fakes, but it's not where the value comes from.

options.text: People trust the RBI and government behind it
options.why: Right. Money is a shared belief backed by law and a trusted central bank.

steps.title: UPI in real life
steps.realLife: UPI moves money between bank accounts in seconds. The money is still rupees held in banks, which are regulated by the RBI.
steps.mission: Ask a parent how they paid for things when they were your age.
steps.deeper: Every UPI payment needs a bank account and a UPI PIN. Never share your PIN or an OTP with anyone: real banks and apps never ask for them.

lessons.title: Money is a tool
lessons.subtitle: Earn, spend, save, invest
lessons.capability: Tell needs from wants, and saving from investing.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Money isn't the goal. It's a tool for the life you want.
There are four things you can do with it.

items.title: Earn
items.text: Swap your time and skills for money: a part-time job, tutoring, a small business.

items.title: Spend
items.text: Needs first (food, travel to school), wants second (that new game skin).

items.title: Save
items.text: Keep money safe for later and for emergencies.

items.title: Invest
items.text: Put money to work so it can grow for Future You.

steps.question: Which of these is a NEED?

options.why: Nice to have, but your current shoes still work. That's a want.
Yes. Getting to school is essential. Needs come before wants.
Fun, but definitely a want.

steps.question: What's the difference between saving and investing?

options.why: Close cousins, but different. Saving keeps money safe; investing puts it to work.

options.text: Investing is only for rich people
options.why: Not true! In India you can start a SIP with as little as ₹100–₹500 a month.

options.text: Saving keeps money safe; investing puts it to work so it can grow
options.why: Exactly. You'll want both: savings for emergencies, investments for Future You.

steps.title: Card: Cash
steps.realLife: Cash is perfect for spending today. For Future You, it has a big problem… Meet The Melt in World 1.
steps.deeper: A common starting rule for a first income is 50% needs, 30% wants and 20% saving and investing. Adjust it to your life; the habit matters more than the exact split.
